To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transverse charge density of the nucleon in the vector mesons region (b {approx} 2 fm) is dominated by {rho} mesons and that the transverse density of the neutron at b{approx} 1.5-1.7 fm is sensitive to the isoscalar vector mesons in the mass region 1-1.2 Gev.

(i) the transverse densities in the nucleon are sensitive to the {omega}-region of the spectral function, (ii) the isovector transverse density at peripheral distances is maximally sensitive to vector mesons and is minimally affected by soft pions, and (iii) the transverse charge density of the neutron is sensitive to the isoscalar region of the spectral function.

the isovector transverse charge density is dominated at distances b {approx}=1 fm by the {rho} resonance, and the isoscalar transverse charge density by higher-mass states up to the {omega}, with the soft-pion region becoming important only at larger b.

the transverse density in the vector mesons is a very clean probe of the t-channel physics of the spacelike electromagnetic form factor.
the transverse charge density can be viewed as a low-pass spectral filter of the nucleon's form factors.
